cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Sit down, love. You've been on the ward all night. I'll bring lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's there a bucket by my chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Just catching a drip. Take the sofa; I've made you a tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll eat upstairs and go straight to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay here. I'll bring your duvet down; upstairs needs a little drying before I put your bed back.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes decision power over B rest, A3 postpones the bucket question and redirects seating, and A5 directs staying downstairs while personally moving bedding.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 bucket inquiry causes A3 small-drip explanation and tray; B4 upstairs plan causes A5 duvet relocation and minimized drying disclosure.

relationship.evidence: B2 notices a practical issue and B4 seeks bed after a ward night; A responds with substantial care rather than exposing B to work.

heightening.evidence: B4 rest solution would reveal the larger problem, so A5 takes on moving bedding and minimizes the displaced bed.

specificity.evidence: A1 overnight ward work supplies the protective motive; B2 bucket and A5 upstairs drying reveal a larger practical problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 little-drying-before-bed-return understatement is earned by B4 upstairs plan and exposes how much A is carrying alone.
